# Proverbs 29 — Disagreement Log
**Generated by:** SOPHIA | **Threshold:** <70% word overlap

---

## 29:2 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | When-[the]-righteous increase the-people rejoice, but-when-[the]-wicked rules the-people groan. |
| LOGOS | When the righteous increase, the people rejoice, but when the wicked rule, the people groan. |
| PNEUMA | When righteous people are in charge, everyone is happy. When the wicked take control, people suffer. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

---

## 29:4 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | A-king by-justice establishes a-land, but-a-man-of contributions tears-it-down. |
| LOGOS | By justice a king builds up the land, but he who exacts gifts tears it down. |
| PNEUMA | A king who practices justice strengthens the nation, but one who demands bribes tears it apart. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 29:5 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | A-man flattering his-neighbor — a-net he-is-spreading upon his-steps. |
| LOGOS | A man who flatters his neighbor spreads a net for his feet. |
| PNEUMA | Flattering your neighbor is actually setting a trap at their feet. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 29:7 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | [The]-righteous knows [the]-cause-of [the]-poor; [the]-wicked does-not-understand knowledge. |
| LOGOS | A righteous man knows the rights of the poor; a wicked man does not understand such knowledge. |
| PNEUMA | A righteous person cares about justice for the poor. The wicked don't even try to understand it. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

---

## 29:8 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | Men-of scoffing fan a-city, but-[the]-wise turn-away anger. |
| LOGOS | Scoffers set a city ablaze, but the wise turn away wrath. |
| PNEUMA | Mockers can set an entire city on fire, but wise people know how to cool things down. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

---

## 29:9 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | A-man wise contending with-a-man foolish — whether-he-rages or-laughs there-is-no rest. |
| LOGOS | If a wise man has an argument with a fool, the fool only rages and laughs, and there is no quiet. |
| PNEUMA | Getting into an argument with a fool is pointless — they'll either rage or laugh, but you'll never reach a resolution. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.
